herdr

herdr.dev · install · quick start · docs · sponsors

English · 简体中文

v.0.4.0.mp4

agent multiplexer that lives in your terminal.

  • every agent at a glance — blocked, working, done. real terminal views, not a wrapped interpretation.
  • detach, agents keep running — reattach from any terminal, or over ssh. sessions survive restarts.
  • agents can use herdr too — a pure socket api: agents spawn panes, read output, wait on each other. agent skill →
  • keyboard and mouse, both first-class — tmux-style prefix keys and click, drag, split. pick per moment, not per tool.
  • plugins — extend panes and workflows. browse the marketplace →
  • one rust binary, no electron — runs in whatever terminal you already use.

install

curl -fsSL https://herdr.dev/install.sh | sh

or brew install herdr · mise use -g herdr · windows beta: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -c "irm https://herdr.dev/install.ps1 | iex" · binaries

then start it where the work lives:

herdr

run your agents, split panes, walk away. ctrl+b q detaches, herdr reattaches. quick start →

docs

everything lives at herdr.dev/docs: quick start · concepts · supported agents · keyboard · configuration · session state · remote · integrations · plugins · socket api

sponsors

herdr is built full-time, in the open. sponsoring directly funds development, stability, and the path to a real agent runtime.

gold

→ become a sponsor · enterprise / partnership: hey@herdr.dev · see SPONSORS.md for tiers. thank you 🐑

agent instructions

if you are an ai agent helping with this repository, read AGENTS.md before making changes and read CONTRIBUTING.md before opening issues or PRs.

development

git clone https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr
cd herdr
cargo build --release

just test        # unit tests
just check       # formatting, tests, and maintenance checks

license

Herdr is licensed under the Apache License 2.0.

releases.name: v0.7.5
releases.body:
### Breaking Changes
- Installed and linked plugins, including their enabled state, are now global to the current user instead of isolated by Herdr session. Plugins installed only in a named session on Herdr 0.7.3 must be installed or linked again. (#1174)

### Added
- Added a live-agent CLI facade with named `start`, atomic `prompt`, logical `send-keys`, and server-owned `wait` workflows. Agent startup targets an existing pane without changing topology, validates the requested interactive agent kind and strict agent name, and accepts native arguments after `--`.
- Added transient declarative Agent view queries through `agent.view.set/clear`; filtered and sorted views now define sidebar, mobile, mouse, and agent-keybind navigation order.
- Added one-shot plugin `[[startup]]` hooks for restoring plugin-owned state after server startup and live handoff.
- Added per-token foreground, bold, and dim styling to expanded Space and Agent sidebar row layouts.
- Added `ui.sidebar_start_collapsed` to launch Herdr with the sidebar collapsed. (#1463)
- Added `ui.prompt_new_workspace_name` to ask for a workspace name before interactive TUI creation.
- Added macOS support for the `HERDR_AGENT=<ag

aiSummary.oneLiner: A specialized, high-performance runtime environment designed specifically for hosting and executing coding agents.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Herdr provides an isolated, robust runtime layer dedicated solely to the execution of autonomous coding agents. It sits between the agent's logic and the host operating system, tightly controlling access to the filesystem, network, and system processes. This architecture ensures that agents can safely execute generated code, run tests, and manipulate files without risking the integrity of the host machine. The runtime provides high-bandwidth IO streams, allowing agents to interact with complex terminal applications or manage long-running background processes seamlessly. By standardizing the execution environment, Herdr allows developers to build agents that perform consistently regardless of the end-user's local setup.
keyFeatures: Isolated Execution: Sandboxes agent actions to prevent accidental deletion of critical files or execution of malicious generated code.
High-Bandwidth IO: Manages complex standard input/output streams, allowing agents to interact seamlessly with interactive CLI tools.
State Persistence: Maintains the agent's working directory and environmental variables perfectly across lengthy, multi-step execution sessions.
Resource Limiting: Enforces hard limits on CPU and memory usage to prevent runaway agent loops from crashing the host system.
Universal Compatibility: Ensures agents run consistently across Windows, macOS, and Linux by abstracting underlying OS discrepancies.

useCases.title: Safe Code Evaluation
useCases.description: AI researchers use the runtime to safely execute and benchmark thousands of AI-generated scripts without risking local system corruption.

useCases.title: Agent Deployment
useCases.description: Developers bundle their custom coding agents with Herdr to guarantee they function correctly on any client's machine.

useCases.title: Automated Build Pipelines
useCases.description: DevOps teams grant agents access to specific, sandboxed build environments to automatically debug failing CI processes.

useCases.title: Interactive Tooling
useCases.description: Engineers build agents that can autonomously navigate complex interactive tools like vim or database prompts via the specialized IO streams.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: AI engineers, tool builders, and researchers developing complex, autonomous coding agents that require safe and consistent execution environments. Requires solid understanding of system processes and sandboxing.
